newsitem.title: USA: Famous Dave's Q2 shr loss $0.15 vs $0.06.
newsitem.headline: Famous Dave's Q2 shr loss $0.15 vs $0.06.

text.p: Famous Dave's of America Inc. (NASDAQ:DAVE) Thursday reported net sales for the 13 weeks ended June 29, 1997, of $3,797,462, compared with net sales of $716,479 for the 13 weeks ended June 30, 1996, an increase of 430 percent.

Restaurant operating income for the 13 weeks ended June 29, 1997, increased 130 percent to $456,151, compared with restaurant operating income of $197,717 for the year-ago period. The net loss for the quarter was $921,391, or 15 cents per share on 6,219,044 weighted average shares outstanding, compared with a net loss of $137,755, or 6 cents per share on 2,214,423 weighted average shares outstanding in 1996. Sales and Restaurant Operating Income Strong

"Famous Dave's achieved strong sales and restaurant-level profitability during the second quarter and first half of 1997," said Dave Anderson, chairman of Famous Dave's. "At the same time, we continued the development of our infrastructure to support our rapid expansion, which is the primary reason for our current net loss at the bottom line. Also during the quarter, we were very pleased with our openings in Maple Grove and St. Paul."
The company noted that prior to June 1996, only its original Linden Hills unit was open, and the increase in net sales and restaurant operating income reflect the following restaurant openings:
Calhoun BBQ and Blues Club September 1996

Restaurant costs and expenses for the 13 weeks ended June 29, 1997, were in-line with expectations at $3,341,311, or 88 percent of sales, compared with $518,762, or 72 percent of sales for the same period in 1996.

Restaurant costs and expenses for the 26 weeks ended June 29, 1997, were also in-line with expectations at $5,273,227, or 87 percent of sales, compared with $770,755, or 77 percent of sales for the same period in 1996. The increase in both periods was primarily attributable to higher pork prices and the impact of pre-opening expenses.

Restaurant operating margins before pre-opening expenses in 1997 were 19.5 percent during the quarter and 17.5 percent year-to-date. "Our restaurant operating margins before pre-opening expenses compare very favorably to those achieved by the strongest competitors in our industry," said Anderson.

The company noted that general and administrative expenses are decreasing as a percentage of sales. General and administrative expenses for the 13 weeks ended June 29, 1997, were $1,497,795, or 39 percent of sales, compared with $315,877, or 44 percent of sales for the 13 weeks ended June 30, 1996.

General and administrative expenses for the 26 weeks ended June 29, 1997, were $2,564,805, or 42 percent of sales, compared with $601,824, or 60 percent of sales for the 26 weeks ended June 30, 1996. The dollar increase in general and administrative expenses was primarily attributable to costs associated with the development of the company's infrastructure to support its growth.

Results for the quarter were negatively impacted by a change in accounting for pre-opening costs which, beginning in the second quarter 1997, are now charged to expense in the month each new unit opens. Previously, pre-opening expenses were deferred and amortized over the 12-month period following each new unit opening.

This change negatively affected earnings by approximately $230,000, or 4 cents per share, in the quarter ended June 29, 1997. Sales for the 26 weeks ended June 29, 1997, increased 500 percent to $6,038,145, compared with sales of $1,006,867 for the 26 weeks ended June 30, 1996.

Restaurant operating income for the 26-week period increased 224 percent to $764,918 from $236,112 for the year-ago period. The year-to-date loss was $1,540,678, or 25 cents per share on 6,218,233 weighted average shares outstanding, compared with a net loss of $388,203, or 18 cents per share on 2,214,423 weighted average shares outstanding in 1996. Rapid Expansion Continues

"Famous Dave's is continuing to aggressively execute its expansion plans both through new restaurant openings and the continued development of a franchise system that will allow the many interested developers to share in our concept and help build our brand," continued Anderson.
"We expect to file an offering circular during the third quarter in order to initiate the development of Famous Dave's as a nationwide franchise.

"Already in July we have successfully opened two additional Famous Dave's: one in Apple Valley, Minn., and the other in Stillwater, Minn. Both opened on the same day, July 18, to strong customer demand.

"While our growth to date has been gratifying, more significantly we have built the management team and much of the infrastructure to support the development of a strong nationwide network of both company-owned and franchised Famous Dave's.

"We look forward to initially achieving this goal through continued expansion in the Midwest, including Chicago. We are increasingly excited by our success in bringing great food, blues music and atmosphere to an increasing number of satisfied customers." Move to Nasdaq National Market System

The company noted that as of Friday, July 25, 1997, Famous Dave's common stock will commence trading on the Nasdaq National Market System. "We are pleased to have so quickly met the financial and other requirements for listing on the Nasdaq National Market System," Anderson said.

Famous Dave's develops, owns and operates Americana roadhouse-style barbecue restaurants under the name Famous Dave's. The company now operates seven Famous Dave's restaurants, with an additional nine locations in development.
